title: Venetian despatches in ASVe Busta 30: Alvise Mocenigo, Rome 25 Apr 1558 (DECODE R1873) and Sebastiano Foscarini, Paris 11 Sep 1680 (DECODE R1871)

documents.shelfmark: ASVe, IT ASVe 0045 010 Busta 30 ff. 4-6 (DECODE R1873)
documents.route: Alvise Mocenigo, Venetian ambassador at Rome, to Doge Lorenzo Priuli

plaintext.source: Paolo Bonavoglia, 'Decifra dispacci veneziani', crittologia.eu (Wayback snapshot 2025-06-22)

transcription.notes: Images viewed here (DECODE login); transcription not redone.

documents.shelfmark: ASVe, IT ASVe 0045 010 Busta 30 f. 4 (DECODE R1871)
documents.route: Sebastiano Foscarini, Venetian ambassador in France, to the Doge (despatch no. 117)

plaintext.source: Paolo Bonavoglia, 'Decifra dispacci veneziani', crittologia.eu (listed; not retrievable 2026-09-22)

transcription.source: transcribed here from deskewed line strips (two agents)
transcription.notes: First pass; 3/5 and 2/0 confusions likely, L22 middle weakest; 1,839 digits.

system.summary: R1873: Venetian nomenclator, each sign a base letter with a superscript letter (letters, syllables, words), Bonavoglia's 'Cifra n. 3' family. R1871: Foscarini's 1680s numerical nomenclator (Paris and Madrid). R1871 segmented as 3-digit groups (first digit 1-5, second 1-6, third 0-9; rare digits 0/7/8/9 only in third place), 211 distinct; not alphabetically ordered.
system.sibling_key: Bonavoglia's reconstructed Venetian keys (Cifra n. 3 family; Foscarini 1680s)
system.notes: The two records are unrelated despatches 122 years apart; DECODE's 1555/England metadata on R1871 appears copied from R1872.

prior_solution.where: crittologia.eu/critto/venezia_nomenclatore.html (Bonavoglia); pointer in Tomokiyo's note on DECODE R1872

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R1871-R1873 images with the DECODE cookie and viewed them; identified Mocenigo (Rome 25 Apr 1558) and Foscarini (Paris 11 Sep 1680, no. 117) from signatures and dockets.
Grepped CSP Venice vi April 1558 on BHO for the Mocenigo despatch.
Followed Tomokiyo's R1872 note to Bonavoglia's page (live site HTTP 500); Wayback copy holds the R1873 transcription and full decipherment and lists the Foscarini 1680-09-11 despatch.
Transcribed R1871's cipher page (23 lines, 1,839 digits) from deskewed strips with two agents.
Tested pair and self-delimiting ([1-4]*[5-0], [1-5]*[6-0]) segmentations; homophonic annealing gave no Italian.
Found rare digits 0/7/8/9 fixed mod 3 within lines: 3-digit groups; DP segmentation to 612 groups, 211 distinct.
Monotone (ordered syllabary) annealer, 12 seeds, clean Italian 4-gram; synthetic ordered control recovered in part, real text not.
Sukhotin vowel test: vowel-like and consonant-like codes interleave, so the table is not alphabetical.
Free letter-per-code and letter/syllable annealers, 14 seeds: seed-dependent overfit gibberish.
Searched for the key and Bonavoglia's Foscarini page: DECODE Venetian keys R1788-R1790 (16th c., no match); crittologia storia page 404/refused, not archived.

outcome.method_basis: R1873 (Mocenigo, Rome 1558) was read from Paolo Bonavoglia's published decipherment on crittologia.eu; R1871 (Foscarini, Paris 1680) was transcribed and attacked ciphertext-only without result, and Bonavoglia's decipherment of it could not be retrieved.
outcome.notes: R1873 read by Bonavoglia (nothing added). R1871 attempted, not read: 3-digit homophonic/syllabic nomenclator, one page too short to solve blind; key and Bonavoglia's decipherment unreachable.
